question: Can I switch my Canadian passport back to my previous name without submitting a new application?
generated_answer:
Yes, you can switch your Canadian passport back to your previous name without submitting a new application. However, you will need to provide proof of your previous name, such as a marriage certificate or divorce decree, and pay the applicable fee. You can also request a change of name on your passport if you have legally changed your name through a court order or other legal process.

It's important to note that if you have already applied for a new passport with your new name, you will need to cancel that application and submit a new one with your previous name. You may also need to provide additional documentation to support your request for a name change.

To request a name change on your Canadian passport, you can contact the Passport Canada office or apply online through the Government of Canada's website. You will need to provide the required documentation and pay the applicable fee, which is currently $50 for a name change on a passport.

It's also worth noting that if you have any travel plans, you should ensure that your passport name matches the name on your travel documents, such as your airline ticket or visa, to avoid any issues during travel.

If you have any further questions or concerns, I would recommend contacting Passport Canada or the Government of Canada's website for more information and guidance.
